findings.text: Exposes core reinitialization helpers for hotplug reuse: one to reset a node descriptor and its zones to empty state reporting resource exhaustion on per cpu allocation failure, one to bind a zone to boot time per cpu sets and batch limits while optionally logging populated zones, and one to detach a reclaimable composite from its list under lock when present.

Exposes node and range hotplug interface: bring a node online under the hotplug guard, report whether self hosted descriptors are usable, add a resource or address range with default onlining, add driver managed ranges with constrained naming and onlining mode, and start offlining a managed range. Variants differ in locking and in whether the caller supplies a resource object.

Node descriptor carries identity, zone array, zone count, reclaim cursors, address span and residency counts, per cpu statistics pointer, wait queues for reclaim and allocation threads plus throttling, and an embedded reclaim vector. Initialization sets up resize support, reclaim locks, compaction waiting, the wait queues and the reclaim vector.

Zone descriptor carries residency counts, ownership link to its node, readable name, exclusion lock with sequence protection, per cpu page sets and statistics, high and batch tuning values, and an isolated block counter. Setup assigns node ownership, name, lock state, per cpu structures and managed count from the caller supplied remainder.

Hotplug uses a descriptor record spanning one block with base and end frame numbers and a free count, linked from the corresponding block device object which also stores the requested onlining mode. Creation duplicates a template descriptor per block for architecture insertion and device creation; removal clears the link, tears down devices and architecture state, then releases the descriptor.

Reusing a node descriptor for hotplug first refreshes internal objects, allocates per cpu statistics when still bound to the boot instance, zeroes zone count and reclaim cursors and address span, folds leftover per cpu deltas into node counters before clearing them, and resets every zone to zero resident pages. Zones are then treated as empty until later onlining populates them.

Hotplug granularity is constrained: add paths require a non empty range aligned to the block size in both start and length, offlining requires a non empty pageblock aligned start with an end aligned to section granularity and forbids holes or spans covering more than one zone. Self hosted descriptor pages must additionally cover whole pageblocks and leave usable payload.

Self hosted descriptors are allowed only when a runtime switch is enabled, the descriptor size is page aligned, its page count is pageblock aligned and smaller than the whole block, and the architecture accepts the size for single table mapping with complete table coverage. Otherwise the add path uses plain architecture insertion without per block descriptors.

Early boot parsing enables a movable node flag unconditionally reporting success, and a range walk callback accumulates the visited page count into caller storage reporting continuation. The offlining path uses the accumulator to compare usable resident pages against the requested span to detect holes.

Node bring up is idempotent: already online nodes report success immediately, otherwise the descriptor is initialized and rebuilt, with failure reported as resource exhaustion. The caller chooses whether to mark online and register; one wrapper performs marking under the hotplug guard while the internal helper used during range addition leaves marking to its caller.

Range addition validates alignment, resolves a group identifier to a node when flagged and rejects impossible nodes, enters the hotplug guard, optionally records the range, ensures the node is initialized, then branches to per block descriptor creation or plain insertion followed by device creation. On success it links blocks under the node, records firmware state for system ranges, merges resources when allowed and walks blocks to online them; failures unwind devices, architecture state, descriptors, node registration and the recorded range.

Offlining validates granularity and residency, requires absence of holes and single zone coverage, disables per cpu caching and reclaim caching, isolates the interval for offlining, notifies for last memory removal and going offline, then loops over scanning for movable frames, migrating them, dissolving free huge composites and retesting isolation until stable. Success removes isolated pages from the allocator, corrects the isolated block count, re enables caching and subtracts managed and present counts.

Scanning reports the first frame that is reclaim tracked, has movable operations, or is migratable huge, rejects offline pinned frames with busy status and signals absence when none remain, skipping over huge composites by their span. Migration attempts reference acquisition, skips poisoned or unisolatable composites with diagnostics, gathers the rest into a list and moves them with a hotplug reason preferring other nodes while allowing reuse of the same node when no alternative exists, returning survivors to the movable pool on failure.

Hotplug serialization pairs a begin and end around node bring up and around the bulk of range addition until devices exist, with actual page onlining occurring after release. The device level guard wraps whole range addition for plain and driver managed paths. Zone exclusion protects the isolated block correction and reclaim list locking protects detachment, while per cpu and reclaim caches are disabled across the isolation window.

Callable entry points for this lane are node onlining, range addition in resource and address forms, driver managed addition with explicit or default onlining mode, support query for self hosted descriptors, core reinitialization for hotplug reuse, per cpu zone setup, detachment from reclaim lists, and range offlining. Internal validators, per block creators, scanners and migrators are not entry points.

Documented failure modes include allocation failure during node reset, null descriptor on bring up, misaligned or empty ranges, unknown group or impossible node, architecture or device creation errors with staged rollback, partially built per block state unwound on error, unreclaimed descriptor allocation warned at release, busy offline pinned frames, interrupted offlining on pending signals, notifier vetoes, unresolved isolation, and failed isolation or migration with rate limited diagnostics.

Negative results signal distinct outcomes: resource exhaustion for per cpu or descriptor allocation and null node setup, invalid argument for alignment, group, node possibility, hole, multizone or name and mode violations, busy for pinned offline pages, absence when no movable frame remains, and interrupted when a signal is pending during offlining. Non negative bring up results distinguish already present from newly initialized nodes.
